Fixed by pointing the workflow at the repository root; docs/ is retained and stays reachable at /NFL2/docs/. tools/verify.py now fails if pages.yml ever targets docs/ again. Also note this falsified an earlier confirmation claim in this session, which is corrected in the board.

finding: Two computed results contradict conventional assumptions and neither has been resolved: home-field advantage measured on the 2026 log is 0.50 points with a 95% interval of -1.80 to +2.80 (so the customary 2.5 is outside it), and the model's own totals are worse than a do-nothing league mean (11.165 vs 11.078 points of absolute error).

finding: Table filters on the site were being ignored silently. The csv directive parser only accepts a filter clause written as key=value, and dropped any other form without a word, so three published tables had no filter at all: injuries.html 'the six designations that were published' listed all 254 rows instead of the 6 designated ones (and its directive had also lost its closing braces, so for a time the page printed raw template text instead of a table), and suggestions.html Tier 1 and Tier 2 both listed the same 36 rows - the page the owner reads to choose a path showed the same list twice under opposite headings.
evidence: content/injuries.md and content/suggestions.md directives; tools/build_site.py render_csv_table, line 'filters = [f for f in ... if = in f]'; row counts measured by re-rendering each directive in isolation
decision_impact: The unfiltered sections read as if the site had lost the designations and as if every suggestion were tier 1. A silent no-op is the worst failure a filter can have, because the table still renders and the caption still claims a subset.
status: fixed in this build: the parser now raises BuildError for a filter clause that is not key=value or names a missing column; the three directives are repaired (new ':*' style non-blank operator 'field=*', and suggestions tiers filtered on decision); check_site now fails on any stray open brace and verify.py asserts the designation count against the file

finding: Same defect, found from the other side: the deploy mechanism did not match the served tree. This session noticed that pages.yml uploaded docs while the Pages API reported legacy publication from main at /, and that a failed Pages run (PR #30 head 7963d2b7, 22:40Z) changed nothing a reader could see. Session 8361cc7a found the same thing by fetching the site and proved it the only way that counts - GET /defense.html returned 200 while GET /line-origination.html returned 404 - recorded as FL-26 and fixed in PR #34, which repointed the artifact at the repository root behind a pre-flight check. What is left is mine to record: the two mechanisms still both run, and no session in this sandbox has ever seen its own site, because egress excludes github.io.
evidence: gh api repos/kanlerxz87-cyber/NFL2/pages -> build_type legacy, source main, path /; gh api pages/builds -> 'built' for 9af81a7f at 22:52:40Z and for 57e6888c at 22:58:23Z; gh run list --workflow pages.yml -> success on 01aeb04c, 40075341, 2386c510 and 9af81a7f, then FAILURE on 57e6888c at 22:58:01Z; gh run view 43324685409 --json jobs -> every step succeeded including actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3, only 'Run actions/deploy-pages@v4' failed; the job annotation reads 'Error: No artifacts named "github-pages" were found for this workflow run' with the action's own advice 'Fetching artifact metadata failed. Is githubstatus.com reporting issues with API requests, Pages, or Actions? Please re-run the deployment at a later time.'; gh run rerun and gh workflow run pages.yml both refused from this sandbox with HTTP 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'; then: gh run list for 4b897e55 -> 'GitHub Pages: completed/success' and 'pages-build-deployment: completed/success', gh api pages/builds -> built at 23:05:48Z
decision_impact: Two mechanisms deploy the same site and only one of them is load-bearing. While Pages is in legacy mode the red Actions run is noise, but it is noise with teeth: a session that treats 'the Pages workflow is green' as the deployment proof will now sometimes see red on a commit that published fine, and a session that treats a green run as proof will be wrong in the other direction, because the bytes are served by the legacy build. Also unfixable from a sandbox: no agent session here can re-run a failed workflow or dispatch one, so a genuinely stuck deploy has to be retried by a push or by you. Practical rule for the next session, now recorded: one red GitHub Pages run is not evidence of an outage - read the Pages API build record for the same commit before believing either. And no agent here can re-run a failed workflow (403), so 'retry later' is the only available remedy.
status: RESOLVED AS TRANSIENT, on the evidence this branch asked for. PR #38 merged to main at 4b897e55 and that commit's run of the same workflow passed every step, including the 'Run actions/deploy-pages@v4' step that failed on 57e6888, while the legacy pages-build-deployment also reported built at 23:05:48Z. So: one intermittent artifact-metadata fetch inside deploy-pages, self-clearing on the next push, exactly as the action's own error message advised. The design question in FL-23 (two deploy mechanisms, which one is canonical) is still open and belongs to the deployment owner; this row is closed.

finding: The published standings table was one game stale when this session opened the repository. nfl.com made the Week 10 Thursday-night game official (WAS 24, NYG 21) after the last build, and data/standings_2026.csv still carried NYG at 5-2-1 with 182 points for and 172 against, and WAS at 2-5-1 with 172 for and 202 against. evidence: Live nfl.com/standings read at 2026-11-13T06:50Z returns NYG 5-3-1 / 203 / 196 and WAS 3-5-1 / 196 / 223; the repository file held 5-2-1 / 182 / 172 and 2-5-1 / 172 / 202. finding: The Week 11 schedule transcription in this repository disagrees with nfl.com on the broadcaster of two games. The repository has MIA at BUF on FOX and TB at DET on CBS; the official schedule page now shows MIA at BUF on CBS and TB at DET on FOX. The swap is exact - only these two games, both in the 1:00 PM window. Either the league moved them between 12 and 13 November, or the earlier transcription swapped them. Not edited here, because this repository publishes a disagreement with an official page as a flag rather than quietly correcting it.
evidence: nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-11 read at 2026-11-13T06:52Z: "Dolphins at Bills, Sunday, November 22nd, 1:00 PM, CBS" and "Buccaneers at Lions, Sunday, November 22nd, 1:00 PM, FOX". data/schedule_week11_2026.json publishes the same two fixtures with FOX and CBS respectively. All 13 kickoff days and times, both flexed games (JAX at NYG 4:25pm, PIT at PHI 1:00pm) and the six-club bye list agree.
decision_impact: Low - a broadcaster is not a model input. But it is a live disagreement between this site and the league page, and whether to edit two cells or record that the league moved them is a decision a session cannot make on its own, because it cannot tell the two explanations apart.
status: RESOLVED - explained, with two dated official sources. The league's own Week 11 Schedule Change article of 9 November 2026 lists Miami at Buffalo on FOX and Tampa Bay at Detroit on CBS, which is exactly what this repository's transcription holds; the live schedule page read on 13 November lists the same two fixtures as CBS and FOX. The league moved the two broadcasts between 9 and 13 November - the earlier transcription was correct when it was made, so the disagreement was never a transcription error. The canonical Week 11 slate published on this site carries the current values. The pre-existing file data/schedule-week11-2026.json still holds the 9 November values because it feeds the independent Q51 research build; change request CR-0A11-01 is logged for that owner.

finding: The premise behind Q-24 has been wrong since the first session. Every session has recorded that 'this sandbox cannot reach nfl.com', and on that basis every refresh in this repository is hand-transcribed by an agent. Raw HTTPS from the shell does fail - curl to www.nfl.com returns SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL - but the agent's page-fetch path reaches nfl.com, the club sites and github.io-equivalents without trouble. That is how this session re-read the standings, the Week 10 slate, the injury hub (all 7 chunks) and ten club depth charts in one sitting. The consequence is that the repository is not as blind as it says it is, and Q-24's answer has to be split in two: an unattended CI job still cannot fetch, but a session can, and does.
evidence: curl -sS https://www.nfl.com/standings/ from the sandbox -> 'OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to www.nfl.com:443', exit 000, at 2026-11-13T12:36Z. The same URL through the agent's page-fetch path -> HTTP 200 and the full standings table rendered. Ten club depth-chart pages and the 7-chunk injury hub read the same way in the same session.
decision_impact: Do not soften it into 'we cannot fetch'. The distinction is shell vs agent, not sandbox vs internet, and a future session that repeats the blanket claim will under-build. It also means the answer to Q-24 may be 'a session does the refresh on a stated cadence' rather than 'wait for egress', which changes the cost of S-01, S-30, S-35 and S-43 together.

finding: This project's rule is that a table row asserting a fact links an official league page. Ten rows of the new personnel-relief page instead link the club's own site, because there is no league-level depth chart at all - nfl.com/team/depth-chart is a 404. A club-published depth chart on commanders.com is an official NFL-club document, but it is not an nfl.com or operations.nfl.com page, so it sits outside OFFICIAL_HOSTS and would fail a naive reading of rule 1. It is registered as tier B, not tier A, and check_site reports the club hosts as a warning rather than passing silently.

finding: The official injury hub and the clubs' own depth charts disagree about two players' positions, in a way that matters to the join. Miami's chart lists Will Kacmarek as a TE and the hub lists him as a TE too, which is fine - but the Chargers' chart files Daiyan Henley under LB while an official NFL roundup has him traded away from Los Angeles to Denver on 10 November, and he is still printed on the Chargers chart today. The chart is therefore not necessarily current with roster moves, and a chart-derived string can be stale by an unknown number of days even though the practice row beside it is today's.
evidence: chargers.com/team/depth-chart read 2026-11-13T12:51Z prints 'LB | Daiyan Henley | Troy Dye'. nfl.com/news/nfl-news-roundup-latest-league-updates-from-tuesday-nov-10 headlines 'Broncos trade for Chargers' Daiyan Henley'. LAC and BAL are also the two Week 10 clubs the hub reports as 'No Injuries Reported', so there is no practice row to contradict the chart.
decision_impact: A depth chart is a document with its own unexplained vintage; nine of the ten clubs print no date on it at all (only GB prints one). Nothing downstream may treat a chart-derived string as current on the day it was read. This is the object-level form of Q-32 and it argues for S-46.

finding: The personnel-relief join covers 10 of the 28 clubs playing in Week 10, and 85 of the 296 players the official hub lists. The page states this on every unresolved row and publishes a generated table of the 18 uncovered clubs, so nothing is hidden - but the brief asked for the deficiency tracker to work for the league, and it works for a third of it. Transcribing the remaining 18 charts is mechanical and was not done here in one pass because the clubs use different position vocabularies (WAS prints DL where SEA prints DT and NT, and the Rams print no group labels at all), and a fast transcription of 18 charts is exactly how a confident wrong string gets published.
evidence: data/personnel_relief_club_83246f00.csv: 84 club x side rows, of which 54 carry chart_state 'club chart not transcribed this session'. Resolved players: 85 of 296. Clubs covered: WAS NYG NE DET KC GB MIA SEA BAL LAC.
decision_impact: The tracker is useful, not complete, and the difference is the single largest remaining data task. It is also the cheapest: no licence, no entitlement, ten club pages read in twelve minutes. S-39 already asks for the 32-club version; this row records how far it actually got.

finding: The injury hub is volatile enough that a single snapshot cannot distinguish a genuine change of condition from a filing refresh. Between two reads 14 hours apart, 17 players were added, none were removed, and 49 of the 277 players present in both reads changed practice code - 37 toward full participation, 12 away from it - while not one newly listed player carried an injury description. A model that scores the level rather than the delta will price a Wednesday filing as news.
evidence: Compared player by player: data/injuries_wk10_2026_hubrefresh.csv (2026-11-12T22:35Z, 279 rows) against data/availability_watch_c3ec1487.csv (2026-11-13T12:45Z, 296 rows). 49 practice-code changes, 17 additions, 0 removals, 0 new injury cells. Two named cases: Tony Pollard (TEN) full to did-not-practice, the largest downgrade; Kerby Joseph (DET) limited to full and OUT anyway.
decision_impact: Blocking for the surprise signal (S-12) and for gate AW-2: the read cadence has to be a decision (Q-43) before the delta can be treated as information rather than noise.

finding: Both official NFL Game Book PDFs verified for this review carry a notice that other use is prohibited without written permission from the National Football League. Their lineup, substitution, Did Not Play, Not Active, and player-stat sections are relevant to actual game-day status, but the presence of those sections is not permission to bulk fetch, retain, parse, model from, or republish them. No gamebook file or extracted gamebook data has been stored in this repository. See Q-50 and S-58.

finding: 26 of the 31 depth charts transcribed in session 745f788e carry no publication date, so how stale a chart is cannot be measured from the document. Related to FL-50: the 'unofficial' label is not uniform across club pages either, and the two together mean a club chart cannot be dated or graded from its own text. Five do: CHI 31 Oct 2026, GB 10 Nov, LV 10 Nov, SF 10 Nov, TEN 10 Nov. The Chicago chart was already 13 days old when this session read it on 13 November.
evidence: The as_published note recorded for each club in scripts/s745_depth_data.py, read from each club's own /team/depth-chart page on 2026-11-13. 28 of 31 print no date string at all; two of those (GB, CHI) were found by date, and SF, TEN and LV print one, leaving 26 undated. Several clubs print only the disclaimer that the chart is compiled by the club's communications department.
decision_impact: A chart is the club's own ordering at the moment it was published, and a reader cannot tell whether that moment was Tuesday or October. Replacement chains built on an undated chart should be re-read before they are trusted for a live decision; the page says so rather than implying the register is current.

finding: One club prints the same player or omits a player in a way no second official page explains (session 745f788e; FL-49 and FL-53 record the same class of defect found from the cascade side). The Eagles' published chart lists Tanner McKee as the first quarterback, with Cole Payton and Joe Milton behind him, and does not print Jalen Hurts at any depth. The same club's chart prints Jonathan Greenard as a co-first-string at both EDGE positions and leaves one of its three DT columns with no first string at all. These are reproduced exactly as printed; nothing was corrected or filled in.
evidence: https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/team/depth-chart read 2026-11-13. Rows: QB [Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, Joe Milton]; EDGE [Jalyx Hunt / Jonathan Greenard]; EDGE [Nolan Smith Jr. / Jonathan Greenard]; DT ["", Ty Robinson]. The deficiency register counts the blank DT cell as a group with no first string published rather than promoting Ty Robinson into the role.

Which one a model should use is an owner decision (Q-38), not a transcription choice; the register publishes the chart's version and flags the gap instead of resolving it.
